verdicts.reason: The repo part is true: the engine shows F-2-13 has no in-edges and F-5-22's only in-edge is F-2-13, so both are dead. The manual chapter, as transcribed in visadocs.yaml, covers the change to F-2-13 for the investor's spouse and unmarried children. The proposed edge F-2-12 -> F-2-13 is wrong, though: it would have the investor change into their own family member's status. Everywhere else in the graph a family status is entered from the family member's own status (F-2-3 from B-1/D-*/E-*, F-2-71 from F-1/F-3), so F-2-13 should sit next to F-2-12 in the short-term statuses it is offered from. I could not re-fetch the decree (no network, search budget used up); the legal side rests on the repo's transcription of the 2026 manual.
verdicts.correctedFix:

verdicts.reason: The repo part is true. F-2-2 has `age: [0, 18]` and `needs: {parent: korean}`, and rules.js profileFacts() sets parent='none' at 19+. A simulation shows a 25-year-old blocked by both, even with korean:true. Decree 나목 (the person born of a marriage with a Korean national) has no age limit, and the repo's manual extract has a separate case and a 5-year multiple-entry F-2-2 visa for it. Deleting `needs` outright is wrong: the simulation shows F-2-2 then opens even for a reader who answered 'no Korean descent'. Instead use korean:true, which the form defines as 'you, a parent or a grandparent held Korean citizenship', as the adult branch.
verdicts.correctedFix:
# data/visamap.yaml
  F-2-2:
    how: {en: 'Foreign minor child of a Korean citizen, or a person of any age born of a marriage (incl. de facto) with a Korean citizen.', ru: <translate>, uz: <translate>, uz-cyrl: <translate>}
    # delete `age: [0, 18]`
    needs:
    - {parent: korean}   # 가목: minor child of a Korean citizen
    - {korean: true}     # 나목: born of a marriage with a Korean citizen, any age
    next:
    - F-5-3              # keeps its own age [0, 18]
    - to: F-5-1          # onward step for adult holders (see f2#4), shared 4-language note
# F-1.next[to: F-2-2].note.en -> 'For a minor foreign child of a Korean citizen, or a person born of a marriage with a Korean citizen.' (translate ru/uz/uz-cyrl)
# Simulated: age 25 blank -> open (koreansOnly tag); korean:true -> open; korean:false -> blocked; age 16 parent:korean -> open.

verdicts.reason: F-2-R.how.en lists '5 years in a depopulating area' among the entry conditions. The notice (as read from the PDF by the earlier agent) makes it a commitment counted from the day the status is granted. The repo's own extract of the 2026 manual decides it independently: the change list asks only for current proof of residence. It also has a special rule for applicants who could not yet live in the area, who move in within 30 days after the change, which cannot coexist with a 5-year past-residence requirement. The same wrong phrase is in D-10-1 -> F-2-R's note (handled by d10#6), and F-2-R's `income: {gni: 0.7}` looks stale against the living-wage test, which I did not verify.

verdicts.reason: The repo part is true: F-2-T needs [{edu:4,rank:3},{experience:5}], and the simulation shows each branch opens F-2-T on its own. But 'the criteria are conjunctive' is only the base rule. The finding's own evidence says that with income of 4× GNI either the degree or the career leg can be missing, and that the science track uses 5+ years in a PI/책임급 post. So {edu:4,rank:3} alone and {experience:5} alone each match a real route; the current gate is already the narrowest union the engine can express, since it has no income or position fact. The proposed conjunctive gate would wrongly hide F-2-T from 4×-GNI single-leg applicants and from science-track researchers, so only the `how` text should change.
